description.en: Acid rain, recycling, conductors and insulators, circuits and circuit symbols.

html.en: What is acid rain? Acid rain is rain (or snow, fog or mist) that has become acidic because polluting gases have mixed with the water in the clouds. It looks like normal rain — but it damages plants, animals, water and even buildings.

🔥 What causes it?

  • Burning fossil fuels — coal, oil and gas — in factories and power stations.
  • Cars, buses and lorries burning petrol and diesel.
  • A small amount comes from nature too, like volcanoes.

⭐ Learn these two gases by heart:
Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and Nitrogen oxides (NOₓ).
They mix with water in the air and turn into sulfuric acid and nitric acid.
💧 How is acid rain formed? (5 steps)

steps.en: 1🏭Factories and cars burn fossil fuels.
2💨They release sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides into the air.
3☁️The gases rise and mix with water in the clouds.
5🌧️The acid falls as acid rain.

html.en: 💨 The wind can carry those gases very far. Acid rain can fall in a country hundreds of kilometres away from the factory that made the pollution!

rows.en: Damages the leaves, poisons the soil, takes away the goodness plants need. Trees get weak and die.
The water becomes acidic. Fish and frog eggs are damaged and may not hatch.
Their shells are made of calcium. The acid wears the calcium away, and the animal dies.
Slowly eats away stone, metal and paint. Old statues lose their faces!
The same polluted air can make breathing problems worse.

html.en:
🔗 Acid rain breaks the food chain!
In a freshwater lake: shrimps → fish → herons.
If the acid kills the shrimps, the fish have no food and die. Then the herons have no fish to eat, so they die or fly away. One dead animal affects everything above it in the food chain.

✅ Ways to reduce acid rain

  • 🔆 Use renewable energy — solar panels, wind turbines, water power — instead of burning coal.
  • 💡 Use less electricity: turn off lights, TVs and chargers you are not using.
  • 🚲 Walk, cycle, share a car or take the bus instead of one car per person.
  • 🏭 Put filters (scrubbers) on factory chimneys to trap the gases before they escape.
  • 🚗 Use catalytic converters and cleaner fuels in cars.
  • 🌱 Plant trees and add lime to damaged lakes to help them recover.
Exam sentence you can use: "Acid rain is formed when sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning fossil fuels mix with water in the atmosphere and fall as acidic rain."

What is recycling? Recycling means taking used materials and turning them into new things instead of throwing them away as rubbish. An old plastic bottle can become a new bottle — or even a fleece jacket!

❓ Why is recycling important?

  • 🌳 It saves natural resources — trees, oil, sand and metal stay in the ground.
  • ⚡ It saves energy. Making a can from recycled aluminium uses far less energy than making a brand-new one.
  • 🗑️ It means less rubbish in landfills, so we need fewer of them.
  • 💨 It creates less pollution in the air, soil and water.
  • 🐢 It protects animals and their habitats.

📦 Recyclable materials

rows.en:
📄 Paper and cardboard
🍾 Glass bottles and jars
🧴 Plastic bottles and containers
🥫 Aluminium cans and metal tins
📰 Newspapers and magazines

🍌 Food scraps (compost these instead!)
🧻 Dirty tissues and greasy pizza boxes
🍽️ Broken ceramic plates and mirrors
🩹 Nappies and plasters

html.en: Golden rule: rinse it first! Dirty containers with food on them can spoil a whole batch of recycling. 🚿
🔺 The 3 Rs — in this exact order

steps.en:
1🔻REDUCE
Use less in the first place. Take a cloth bag to the shop. Don't buy things you don't need.

2🔁REUSE
Use it again as it is. Refill your water bottle. Turn a jar into a pencil pot. Give clothes away.

3♻️RECYCLE
Turn it into something new. Send paper, glass, plastic and metal to the recycling plant.

html.en: Don't mix these up! 🔁 Reuse = the same object is used again (refilling a bottle). ♻️ Recycle = the object is broken down and made into a new object (a bottle becomes a T-shirt).

🗑️ What happens if we throw away too much trash?

  • Landfills fill up and take over land where plants and animals used to live.
  • Rubbish gives off harmful gases and poisons that leak into the soil and water.
  • Plastic ends up in rivers and the sea. 🐋 Animals eat it or get trapped in it and die.
  • Plastic takes hundreds of years to break down.
Exam sentence you can use: "Recycling is important because it saves natural resources and energy, reduces the amount of rubbish in landfills, and protects animals and the environment from pollution."

⚡ A CONDUCTOR is a material that lets electric current pass through it easily.
🚫 An INSULATOR is a material that does NOT let electric current pass through it.
Easy way to remember: if it is a metal, it is almost always a conductor. If it is not a metal (plastic, rubber, glass, wood), it is almost always an insulator. 🧲

rows.en:
🟠 Copper
⚪ Aluminium
⚙️ Iron and steel
🥇 Gold and silver
✏️ Pencil "lead" (graphite)

🧴 Plastic
🛞 Rubber
🍾 Glass
🪵 Dry wood
🍽️ Ceramic
👕 Cloth and paper
🌬️ Air
The copper carries the electricity; the plastic stops it reaching your hand, so you are safe.
The pan lets heat through to cook; the handle does not, so you don't burn your hand.
The tip does the work; the handle protects the electrician.
Electricity flows inside only — the outside is safe to touch.

html.en: ⚠️ Safety! Your body and water are conductors too. Never touch plugs or switches with wet hands, and never poke anything metal into a socket.
Exam sentence you can use: "Electrical wires are covered with plastic because plastic is an insulator. It stops the electricity from escaping and keeps people safe from electric shocks."

rows.en: A form of energy that can make things work.
The flow of electric charge through a circuit.
A complete path through which electric current can flow.
A source of electrical energy that provides energy to a circuit. (ONE)
Two or more cells connected together to provide electrical energy.
A metal conductor that allows electric current to flow through a circuit.
A component that produces light when electric current flows through it.
A component that opens or closes a circuit.
A circuit with a continuous path that allows electric current to flow.
A circuit with a break in the path, so electric current cannot flow.

html.en: The #1 mistake: a cell is ONE. A battery is TWO OR MORE cells joined together. The thing in your TV remote is really a cell, even though everyone calls it a battery! 😄
⚙️ How does an electric circuit work?

The cell pushes electric charge out. The charge travels along the wires, goes through the bulb (making it light up), and comes all the way back to the cell. It must go round in a complete loop — like a running track. 🏃‍♂️

rows.en: No break anywhere — it goes all the way round.
There is a gap, a loose wire, or the switch is open.

html.en: Why does a bulb not light in an open circuit? Because the path is broken, so the electric current cannot flow through the bulb. Learn that sentence! ✏️
🧪 Go to the 🔌 Circuit Lab tab and build one yourself — it is the fastest way to remember this.

Circuit symbols are simple drawings that represent electrical components. They help us draw circuits clearly and quickly — everyone in the world uses the same ones, so any scientist can read your diagram. 🌍

rows.en: Provides electrical energy to the circuit. One long line + one short thick line.
Provides electrical energy. It is made of two or more cells — so you draw the pattern twice.
Breaks the circuit, so electric current cannot flow. The line is lifted up.
Completes the circuit, so electric current can flow. The line is flat.
Changes electrical energy into movement. A circle with an M inside.
Connects the components and allows electric current to flow. A straight line — use a ruler! 📏

html.en:
Cell vs Battery symbol: count the pairs of lines!
1 pair = cell. 2 or more pairs = battery.
Bulb vs Motor: both are circles. X inside = bulb (light 💡). M inside = motor (movement ⚙️).

Follow the wire with your finger, starting at the cell. Say the name of every symbol you pass. When you get back to the cell — that's the whole circuit! If your finger has to jump a gap, the circuit is open and nothing will work.
Rules for drawing: ✏️ use a ruler for every wire · draw symbols only, never the real objects · make corners into right angles · label each component.
🃏 Go to the 🎮 Games tab and win Symbol Match — after two or three games you will know all 7 symbols without thinking.

The 5 topics on your Final Exam

Click a topic to open it. Read the boxes, look at the pictures, then go to 🎯 Practice and try to get 5 right in a row before moving on.
Burning fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas in factories and cars
Too many trees growing near a lake
Very cold weather in the mountains

stem.en: What is the main cause of acid rain?

hint.en: Think about what comes out of a factory chimney. 🏭

solution.en: Acid rain is caused by burning fossil fuels. Factories, power stations and vehicles release polluting gases into the air.

stem.en: Which TWO gases mix with water in the atmosphere to create acid rain?

hint.en: One starts with S, the other with N.

solution.en: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) mix with water in the clouds and turn into sulfuric acid and nitric acid.

html.en: In the atmosphere, when the gases mix with water in the clouds
At the bottom of the lake

stem.en: Where does acid rain actually form?

hint.en: Look up! ☁️

solution.en: The gases rise up into the atmosphere, mix with water vapour in the clouds, become acid, and then fall as rain.

html.en: The water becomes acidic and fish and frog eggs are damaged
The water turns into ice all year
The lake gets bigger every year

stem.en: Name a harmful effect of acid rain on lakes and rivers.

hint.en: Think about baby animals that have not been born yet. 🐸

solution.en: Acid makes the water acidic. The eggs of fish and amphibians become damaged and may never hatch.

html.en: The acid wears away the calcium in their hard shells
They cannot swim in acid water

stem.en: Why do freshwater shrimps die when a lake becomes acidic?

hint.en: What is their shell made of? 🦐

solution.en: Shrimps have a tough shell made of calcium. The acid wears the calcium away, so the animal dies.

html.en: The fish have no food and die, so then the herons have no food either
Only the shrimps are affected — nothing else changes
The fish start eating the herons

stem.en: In a lake, shrimps → fish → herons. If acid rain kills all the shrimps, what happens?

hint.en: Follow the arrows up the food chain. 🔗

solution.en: This is a food chain. If one living thing is killed, everything above it in the chain loses its food. Damage spreads all the way up.

html.en: It slowly wears away and damages the stone
It makes them shine and look new

stem.en: What does acid rain do to old buildings and statues?

hint.en: Think of a very old statue in a city. 🏛️

solution.en: Acid rain slowly eats away stone, metal and paint. That is why many old statues have lost their faces.

html.en: It damages the leaves and poisons the soil, so trees get weak and die
It changes their leaves to blue

stem.en: What does acid rain do to trees?

hint.en: Is acid good or bad for a plant? 🌳

solution.en: Acid rain damages leaves and takes the goodness out of the soil, so trees become weak and can die.

html.en: Use renewable energy like solar and wind instead of burning coal

stem.en: Which of these is the BEST way to reduce acid rain?

hint.en: Which energy comes from the sun and the wind? 🔆

solution.en: Renewable energy (solar, wind, water) does not burn fossil fuels, so it does not release the gases that cause acid rain.

html.en: Walk, cycle, share a car or take the bus, so fewer fuels are burned
Always travel alone in a big car
Leave the car engine running while you wait

stem.en: How can the way you travel help reduce acid rain?

hint.en: What uses no fuel at all? 🚲

solution.en: Fewer vehicles burning petrol and diesel means fewer polluting gases in the air.

html.en: They trap the harmful gases before they escape into the air
They make the smoke a nicer colour
They make the factory work faster

stem.en: What do filters (scrubbers) on a factory chimney do?

hint.en: Like a net that catches something. 🕸️

solution.en: Filters or "scrubbers" catch sulfur dioxide and other harmful gases before they reach the atmosphere.

html.en: No — it can also fall as snow, fog or mist

stem.en: Does acid rain only fall as rain?

hint.en: Think of all the ways water falls from the sky. ❄️

solution.en: Any acidic precipitation counts: rain, snow, fog and mist can all be acidic.

html.en: True — the wind carries the gases hundreds of kilometres
False — it always falls on the same factory

stem.en: True or false: the pollution that causes acid rain can travel a long way from where it was made.

hint.en: What moves clouds across the sky? 💨

solution.en: Wind carries the gases far away, so acid rain can fall in a completely different region or country.

html.en: Taking used materials and turning them into new products
Burying all rubbish in a big hole

stem.en: What is recycling?

hint.en: Old thing → new thing. ♻️

solution.en: Recycling means used materials are collected, broken down, and made into new things instead of becoming rubbish.

html.en: It saves natural resources and energy, and creates less rubbish and pollution
It makes rubbish disappear by magic

stem.en: Why is recycling important?

hint.en: Think about what stays safe: trees, energy, animals. 🌳

solution.en: Recycling saves trees, oil and metal, uses less energy, reduces landfill and reduces pollution.

stem.en: Which of these can usually NOT be recycled in the normal recycling bin?

hint.en: One of these goes rotten. 🍌

solution.en: Food scraps should be composted, not put in the recycling bin — they can spoil the whole batch.

stem.en: What are the 3 Rs, in the correct order?

hint.en: Which one means "use less in the first place"? That one is first.

solution.en: The order matters! Reduce first (use less), then Reuse (use it again), and only then Recycle.

html.en: Use less in the first place, so there is less waste

stem.en: What does REDUCE mean?

hint.en: Less of something. 🔻

solution.en: Reduce means buying and using less, so less waste is created at all. It is the most powerful R.

html.en: Refilling the same water bottle every day
Melting plastic bottles to make a new jacket
Putting paper in the blue bin
Throwing a bottle in the bin

stem.en: Which of these is an example of REUSE?

hint.en: The object stays the SAME object. 🔁

solution.en: Reuse means using the same object again, just as it is. Refilling a bottle or turning a jar into a pencil pot are reuse.

html.en: Old newspapers being turned into new cardboard boxes
Giving your old coat to your little brother
Using a jam jar to hold your pencils

stem.en: Which of these is an example of RECYCLE (not reuse)?

hint.en: Which one changes into a totally different object?

solution.en: Recycling means the material is broken down and made into a NEW object. The others are all reuse.

html.en: Landfills fill up, the soil and water get polluted, and animals are harmed
Nothing — the Earth absorbs it all
The rubbish turns into soil in one week

stem.en: What happens when we throw away too much trash?

hint.en: Think about where all the rubbish actually goes. 🗑️

solution.en: Landfills take over land, leak harmful liquids and gases, and plastic reaches rivers and oceans where animals eat it or get trapped.

html.en: Less plastic reaches oceans and habitats, so fewer animals eat it or get trapped
It teaches animals to clean up
It has no effect on animals

stem.en: How does recycling help animals and the environment?

hint.en: Think of a turtle and a plastic bag. 🐢

solution.en: Recycling keeps rubbish out of rivers, oceans and forests, protects habitats, and reduces the pollution animals live in.

stem.en: Recycling paper mainly helps to save…

hint.en: What is paper made from? 🌲

solution.en: Paper is made from trees, so recycling paper means fewer trees have to be cut down.

html.en: Much LESS energy than making one from new material

stem.en: Making a new aluminium can from a recycled can uses…

hint.en: Recycling is the energy-saving option. ⚡

solution.en: Recycling aluminium uses far less energy than digging up and processing new metal — that is a big benefit of recycling.

stem.en: Which R should we always try FIRST?

hint.en: The best rubbish is… no rubbish at all!

solution.en: Reduce comes first, because the best kind of waste is the waste that is never created.

html.en: Because food and dirt can spoil the whole batch of recycling
It is not necessary at all

stem.en: Why should you rinse a container before recycling it?

hint.en: Nobody wants a mouldy yoghurt pot in the mix. 🚿

solution.en: Dirty containers can contaminate the other materials, so a quick rinse helps the recycling actually work.

html.en: A material that lets electric current pass through it
A material that blocks electric current
A material that is always soft

stem.en: What is a conductor?

hint.en: It conducts — it lets it through. ⚡

solution.en: A conductor lets electric current pass through it easily. Most metals are good conductors.

html.en: A material that does NOT let electric current pass through it
A material that lets electricity through easily

stem.en: What is an insulator?

hint.en: It insulates — it blocks. 🚫

solution.en: An insulator blocks electric current. Plastic, rubber, glass and dry wood are insulators.

stem.en: Copper is a…

hint.en: What colour metal is inside an electric wire? 🟠

solution.en: Copper is a metal and one of the best conductors — that is why wires are made of it.

stem.en: Plastic is a…

hint.en: It keeps you safe when you touch a wire.

solution.en: Plastic is an insulator. It does not let electricity through, which is why it covers wires.

stem.en: Glass is a…

hint.en: It is not a metal. 🍾

solution.en: Glass is an insulator — electricity cannot pass through it.

stem.en: Aluminium is a…

hint.en: Metals conduct. ⚪

solution.en: Aluminium is a metal, so it is a conductor. Cans and foil are made of it.

stem.en: Rubber is a…

hint.en: Think of an electrician's gloves. 🧤

solution.en: Rubber is an insulator, which is why electricians wear rubber gloves.

stem.en: Which GROUP of materials are usually conductors?

hint.en: Shiny and hard. 🧲

solution.en: Almost all metals conduct electricity. Non-metals like plastic, wood and glass usually do not.

html.en: Because plastic is an insulator, so it stops the electricity reaching us and keeps us safe
Because plastic is a good conductor
To make the wire look colourful only

stem.en: Why are electrical wires covered with plastic?

hint.en: What would happen if the copper was bare? ⚡

solution.en: The copper inside carries the current; the plastic outside is an insulator that stops the electricity escaping, protecting people from electric shocks.

html.en: An insulator, so the heat does not reach your hand and burn you
A conductor, so your hand gets hot faster
A conductor, because it looks nicer

stem.en: If you were designing the HANDLE of a frying pan, would you use a conductor or an insulator?

hint.en: Do you want a hot handle or a cool one? 🍳

solution.en: The handle should be an insulator (plastic or wood) so heat cannot travel to your hand.

html.en: Metal tip = conductor, rubber handle = insulator
Metal tip = insulator, rubber handle = conductor

stem.en: A screwdriver has a metal tip and a rubber handle. Which is which?

hint.en: Metals conduct, rubber blocks. 🪛

solution.en: Metal conducts, rubber insulates. The rubber handle protects the person using it.

html.en: No, because plastic is an insulator
Yes, because plastic is a conductor
Only if the ruler is blue

stem.en: Will electricity flow through a plastic ruler?

hint.en: Plastic blocks electricity. 📏

solution.en: Plastic is an insulator, so electric current cannot pass through it.

html.en: Because water and your body conduct electricity, so you could get a shock
Because water makes plastic a conductor forever
Because it makes the plug cold

stem.en: Why should you never touch a plug with wet hands?

hint.en: Is water a conductor or an insulator? 💧

solution.en: Water and the human body conduct electricity, so wet hands make an electric shock much more likely. Always dry your hands first!

html.en: A form of energy that can make things work

stem.en: What is electricity?

hint.en: It is a form of… ⚡

solution.en: Electricity is a form of energy that can make things work — lights, motors, fridges and phones.

html.en: The flow of electric charge through a circuit

stem.en: What is electric current?

hint.en: Think of a river flowing. 🌊

solution.en: Electric current is the flow of electric charge through a circuit — like water flowing through a pipe.

html.en: A complete path through which electric current can flow

stem.en: What is a circuit?

hint.en: It must be a complete loop. 🔄

solution.en: A circuit is a complete path for electric current — it must go all the way round and come back.

html.en: A source of electrical energy that provides energy to a circuit
Two or more batteries joined together

stem.en: What is a cell?

hint.en: It is just ONE of them. 🔋

solution.en: A cell is a source of electrical energy. Two or more cells joined together make a battery.

html.en: Two or more cells connected together to provide electrical energy
A single cell on its own
A switch that is always on

stem.en: What is a battery?

hint.en: How many cells? More than one! 🔋🔋

solution.en: A battery is TWO OR MORE cells connected together. One on its own is a cell.

html.en: It produces light when electric current flows through it

stem.en: What does a bulb do in a circuit?

hint.en: It glows. 💡

solution.en: A bulb changes electrical energy into light energy when current flows through it.

html.en: It opens or closes a circuit

stem.en: What does a switch do?

hint.en: On… off… on… off. 🎚️

solution.en: A switch opens the circuit (current stops) or closes it (current flows). It turns things on and off.

html.en: A circuit with a continuous path that allows electric current to flow
A circuit with a break in it
A circuit made only of plastic

stem.en: What is a complete circuit?

hint.en: No breaks anywhere! ✅

solution.en: A complete circuit has a continuous path with no break, so current can flow and the bulb lights up.

html.en: A circuit with a break in the path, so current cannot flow
A circuit made of copper only

stem.en: What is an open circuit?

hint.en: Something is missing or lifted up. ❌

solution.en: An open circuit has a break — a gap, a loose wire, or an open switch — so current cannot flow.

html.en: Because the path is broken, so electric current cannot flow through the bulb
Because the bulb is too old
Because the wires are too short
Because the cell is upside down

stem.en: Why does a bulb NOT light up in an open circuit?

hint.en: What must the current have all the way round? 🔄

solution.en: The current needs a complete path. If the path is broken, no current reaches the bulb, so it stays off.

html.en: Because metal is a conductor, so current can flow through it

stem.en: Why are wires made of metal?

hint.en: Conductor or insulator? ⚡

solution.en: Metal is a conductor, so it allows electric current to flow through the circuit.

html.en: A cell, wires and a bulb
A ruler, a pencil and a rubber

stem.en: Name three components of a simple electric circuit.

hint.en: Energy source + path + something that works. 🔋➖💡

solution.en: A simple circuit needs a cell (energy), wires (to carry the current) and a bulb (to do the job). A switch is often added too.

stem.en: Which will make the bulb light up?

hint.en: Closed = joined = current flows. 🔒

solution.en: A closed switch completes the circuit so current can flow and the bulb lights.

html.en: The circuit becomes open, so the current stops and the bulb goes off

stem.en: What happens if you remove one wire from a working circuit?

hint.en: You just made a gap. ✂️

solution.en: Removing a wire creates a break, making the circuit open. Current cannot flow, so the bulb goes out.

html.en: False — a complete circuit has NO break
True, but only with a battery
Only if there is a motor

stem.en: True or false: a complete circuit has a broken path.

hint.en: Careful — this one is a trick. 🤔

solution.en: False! A complete circuit has a continuous path with no break. It is the OPEN circuit that has a break.

stem.en:
Which component does this symbol represent?
[circuit symbol: cell]

hint.en: Count the pairs of lines. Only one pair!

solution.en: One long thin line + one short thick line = a CELL. It provides electrical energy to the circuit.

stem.en:
Which component does this symbol represent?
[circuit symbol: battery]

hint.en: Count the pairs of lines. Two pairs!

solution.en: Two pairs of lines = a BATTERY, because a battery is two or more cells connected together.

stem.en:
Which component does this symbol represent?
[circuit symbol: bulb]

hint.en: A circle with a cross. What gives light? 💡

solution.en: A circle with an X inside = a BULB. It changes electrical energy into light energy.

stem.en:
Which component does this symbol represent?
[circuit symbol: motor]

hint.en: M is for… ⚙️

solution.en: A circle with an M inside = a MOTOR. It changes electrical energy into movement.

stem.en:
Which component does this symbol represent?
[circuit symbol: open switch]

hint.en: Is the line flat or lifted up? 🔓

solution.en: Two dots with the line LIFTED UP = an OPEN switch. It breaks the circuit, so current cannot flow.

stem.en:
Which component does this symbol represent?
[circuit symbol: closed switch]

hint.en: The line is flat and joins both dots. 🔒

solution.en: Two dots joined by a FLAT line = a CLOSED switch. It completes the circuit, so current can flow.

html.en: It changes electrical energy into movement
It changes electrical energy into light

stem.en: What is the function of a MOTOR in a circuit?

hint.en: What does a motor make things do? ⚙️

solution.en: A motor changes electrical energy into movement — it makes things spin or move.

html.en: It changes electrical energy into light energy
It changes electrical energy into movement

stem.en: What is the function of a BULB in a circuit?

hint.en: It shines. 💡

solution.en: A bulb changes electrical energy into light energy.

html.en: Because symbols are simple, clear and quick to draw, and everyone understands them
Because drawing objects is not allowed

stem.en: Why do scientists use circuit symbols instead of drawing the real objects?

hint.en: Which is faster to draw: a real light bulb or a circle with an X? ⏱️

solution.en: Symbols are simple drawings that let us show circuits clearly and quickly — and every scientist in the world uses the same ones.

stem.en: You want the current to STOP flowing. Which symbol would you draw?

hint.en: Which switch makes a gap? 🔓

solution.en: An open switch breaks the circuit, so the current stops flowing.

html.en: It connects the components and allows current to flow through the circuit
It opens and closes the circuit

stem.en: What is the function of a WIRE in a circuit?

hint.en: It joins everything together. ➖

solution.en: A wire is a metal conductor. It connects the components and allows electric current to flow.

html.en: A ruler, so the lines are straight

stem.en: When you draw a circuit diagram, what should you use to draw the wires?

hint.en: Straight lines need a… 📏

solution.en: Always use a ruler. Circuit diagrams use straight lines and right-angled corners, and every component should be labelled.

html.en: No, because the open switch breaks the circuit
Only if you add a motor

stem.en: A circuit shows a cell, a bulb and an open switch. Will the bulb light up?

hint.en: Follow the path with your finger — is there a gap? 🔓

solution.en: An open switch means the circuit is not complete, so current cannot flow and the bulb stays off.

stem.en: How many cells are shown in a battery symbol that has TWO pairs of lines?

hint.en: One pair = one cell. 🔋

solution.en: Each pair of lines (one long thin + one short thick) is one cell. Two pairs = 2 cells = a battery.

html.en:
🗓️ A 5-day plan to be ready

Short study sessions beat one long panic session. 25–35 minutes a day is plenty.

⭐ The 10 marks students throw away every year

  1. Saying acid rain is caused by "dirty water" — it's caused by burning fossil fuels.
  2. Forgetting the two gases: sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides.
  3. Writing the 3 Rs in the wrong order. It is Reduce → Reuse → Recycle.
  4. Mixing up Reuse (use it again as it is) and Recycle (make it into something new).
  5. Saying glass is a conductor. Glass is an insulator. Metals are the conductors.
  6. Mixing up cell (one) and battery (two or more cells).
  7. Saying a complete circuit has a break. A complete circuit has NO break.
  8. Drawing the real objects instead of the symbols in a circuit diagram.
  9. Drawing an open switch when the question asked for a closed one (or the other way round).
  10. Leaving a question blank. Always write something — you can't get marks for an empty line.
The night before: don't learn anything new. Re-read the blue rule boxes in Learn, do 10 quick questions in Practice, then stop. Sleep is worth more marks than another hour of studying. 😴
In the exam: read every question twice. Underline the question word (name, explain, draw, why). If it says explain, write a because… sentence. If it says draw, use a ruler and label everything. 📏
